svg.title: Figure 6-1 · Defence in depth per safety goal
svg.desc: Matrix of safety goals by protection layer (host SoC, safety envelope, vehicle ECUs, driver, plus operation) with TSR counts, status at the baseline and SM types. SG-01 ASIL C: host 12 TSRs partly, envelope 44 TSRs partly, vehicle 2 EXT TSRs and 1 AoUs assumed, driver 7 hazardous events rated by controllability, operation 6 TSRs; SG-02 ASIL C: host 28 TSRs partly, envelope 20 TSRs partly, vehicle 2 EXT TSRs and 2 AoUs assumed, driver 8 hazardous events rated by controllability, operation 3 TSRs; SG-03 ASIL C: host 9 TSRs partly, envelope 40 TSRs partly, vehicle 2 EXT TSRs and 3 AoUs assumed, driver 7 hazardous events rated by controllability, operation 5 TSRs; SG-04 ASIL B: host 12 TSRs partly, envelope 39 TSRs partly, vehicle 2 EXT TSRs and 3 AoUs assumed, driver 5 hazardous events rated by controllability, operation 5 TSRs; SG-05 ASIL B: host 7 TSRs partly, envelope 32 TSRs partly, vehicle 4 EXT TSRs and 3 AoUs assumed, driver 4 hazardous events rated by controllability, operation 5 TSRs; SG-06 ASIL C: host 28 TSRs partly, envelope 18 TSRs partly, vehicle 1 EXT TSRs and 2 AoUs assumed, driver 4 hazardous events rated by controllability, operation 3 TSRs; SG-07 ASIL B: host 6 TSRs partly, envelope 28 TSRs partly, vehicle 1 EXT TSRs and 1 AoUs assumed, driver 1 hazardous events rated by controllability, operation 8 TSRs; SG-08 ASIL A: host 9 TSRs partly, envelope 0 TSRs none, vehicle 0 EXT TSRs and 1 AoUs assumed, driver 2 hazardous events rated by controllability, operation 1 TSRs.
svg.text: Figure 6-1 · Defence in depth per safety goal
Protection layers between a fault and the hazard, inside to outside, with the TSRs and assumptions that make up each layer and their status at the baseline.
each layer can stop the fault before the next; inside → outside
E-03 · E-04a · E-05 · P-SW, P-HW, HAR
EPS · PCM · brake · PCS · alloc. EXT

Bar: the TSRs of the cell by status. Monospace: the most frequent SM types of those TSRs (WP-S-02 §2.2: LIM limiter, GATE gating, PLB plausibility, TMO timeout, FR fault reaction, CFG configuration lock, WRN warning …).

Status rule, per TSR from baseline_impl: “Implemented …”/“Met …” without a qualifier = implemented; “Partial”, “Partly” or a qualified one (no rationale, reference build only, subset, via another TSR) = partly;
“Not …”, “Unknown”, “Not verified” = not implemented; EXT or “Unverified (AOU-…)” = assumed; OPS procedures = partly (“Blocked”: not implemented).
A cell is implemented only if all its TSRs are, not implemented only if all are not, otherwise partly. A TSR allocated to two layers counts in both.
Nothing here is verified: implemented means the baseline code does it. HARA C ratings, ASILs and AoUs are proposals.
